page.text:
Beyond mapping individual points, a function induces actions on the power
sets of its domain and codomain:
- The *direct image* $f[X]$ pushes a subset $X \subseteq A$ forward into
  $B$, collecting all evaluations $f(x)$ for $x \in X$.
- The *preimage* (or inverse image) $f^{-1}[Y]$ pulls a subset
  $Y \subseteq B$ back into $A$, collecting all inputs that map into $Y$.
  Crucially, the preimage $f^{-1}[Y]$ is well-defined for *any* function,
  requiring no invertibility of $f$.
